answer_text:
Let

\[
D_n=X_2-X_1.
\]

The Beta distributions can be written as

\[
X_1\sim \text{Beta}(1,n),\qquad X_2\sim \text{Beta}(n,1).
\]

Their survival/tail probabilities are

\[
\Pr(X_1>u)= (1-u)^n,\qquad 0<u<1,
\]

and since \(1-X_2\sim \text{Beta}(1,n)\),

\[
\Pr(1-X_2>u)= (1-u)^n,\qquad 0<u<1.
\]

Define

\[
Z_n=1-X_2.
\]

Then \(Z_n\sim \text{Beta}(1,n)\), and because \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) are independent, \(X_1\) and \(Z_n\) are independent. Thus

\[
D_n=X_2-X_1=(1-Z_n)-X_1=1-(X_1+Z_n).
\]

Now for any \(0<\varepsilon<1\),

\[
\Pr\bigl(|D_n-1|>\varepsilon\bigr)
=
\Pr(X_1+Z_n>\varepsilon).
\]

By the union bound,

\[
\Pr(X_1+Z_n>\varepsilon)
\le
\Pr\left(X_1>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)
+
\Pr\left(Z_n>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right).
\]

Using the tail probability of \(\text{Beta}(1,n)\),

\[
\Pr\left(X_1>\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)
=
\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)^n,
\]

and similarly for \(Z_n\). Therefore

\[
\Pr\bigl(|D_n-1|>\varepsilon\bigr)
\le
2\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)^n
\longrightarrow 0.
\]

Hence

\[
D_n=X_2-X_1 \xrightarrow{p} 1.
\]

Convergence in probability implies convergence in distribution, so the limiting distribution is a point mass at \(1\). Its limiting CDF is

\[
F_\infty(t)=
\begin{cases}
0, & t<1,\\
1, & t\ge 1.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{X_2-X_1 \xrightarrow{d} \delta_1}
\]

where \(\delta_1\) is the Dirac distribution, i.e. a degenerate distribution equal to \(1\) almost surely.

As a related non-degenerate scaling, since \(nX_1\Rightarrow E_1\) and \(nZ_n\Rightarrow E_2\) with \(E_1,E_2\stackrel{\text{iid}}{\sim}\text{Exp}(1)\),

\[
n\bigl(1-(X_2-X_1)\bigr)
=
n(X_1+Z_n)
\Rightarrow E_1+E_2\sim \text{Gamma}(2,1).
\]
